newsitem.title: USA: Edison Mission starts building Turkey plant.
newsitem.headline: Edison Mission starts building Turkey plant.

text.p: Edison Mission Energy, an Edison International company, said on Monday Doga Enerji AS completed financing and began building the $182.4 million Doga Enerji Cogeneration project in the Esenyurt suburb of Istanbul, Turkey.
Doga Enerji AS is a joint venture company 80 percent owned by Edison Mission and 20 percent owned by Turkish developers.

The 180-megawatt, natural gas-fuelled Doga project would provide both hot water to heat 14,000 new homes and electricity needed by the Turkish national electric utility, it said. The project would begin to provide heat for homes in the summer of 1997. Construction was due to be completed by late 1998, it said.
Project costs will be financed via $45.6 million in equity contributions from shareholders and with $136.8 million in non-recourse project financing, the company said.
